story.iWant: specialized synthesis agent that combines retrieval and analysis results into coherent answers
story.soThat: multi-step workflows produce natural language responses with proper source attribution

tasks.task: Implement synthesis_agent function with @tool decorator (4 hours) - Create raglite/agentic/agents/synthesis_agent.py file - Implement @tool async def synthesis_agent(retrieval_results, analysis_results, query) with AWS Strands decorator - Define SynthesisResult Pydantic model in raglite/agentic/state.py (answer, reasoning_steps, sources, metadata) - Implement multi-source aggregation logic (combine retrieval + analysis results) - Add error handling for invalid inputs or missing data (return error metadata)

Integrate Claude Sonnet for high-quality synthesis (3 hours) - Import Claude client from raglite/shared/clients.py - Create structured prompt templates for synthesis tasks - Implement LLM synthesis call with Claude Sonnet model - Parse LLM response and extract reasoning steps + citations - Add retry logic for Claude API errors (429/500 status codes) - Validate citation preservation and factual accuracy

Create unit tests for synthesis agent (3 hours) - Create tests/unit/agentic/test_synthesis_agent.py - Mock Claude API to return synthetic synthesis results - Test synthesis of retrieval results only (basic summary) - Test synthesis of retrieval + analysis results (complex workflow) - Test source citation preservation from all upstream agents - Test handling of conflicting information from multiple sources - Test error handling (invalid inputs, missing data, LLM API failure) - Validate test execution time <100ms (no real LLM calls)

Create integration test for complete 3-agent workflow (4 hours) - Update tests/integration/test_analysis_agent_workflow.py to use real synthesis_agent - Implement full Retrieval → Analysis → Synthesis workflow test - Use real Qdrant instance (requires docker-compose up -d) - Use real Claude Sonnet for synthesis (budget LLM calls) - Remove MockSynthesisAgent usage from existing tests - Test complete workflow coordination via AWS Strands orchestrator - Validate workflow execution time <8s - Validate all source citations preserved in final output

Update orchestrator configuration (1 hour) - Add synthesis_agent to orchestrator tools list in raglite/agentic/orchestrator.py - Update orchestrator system prompt to include synthesis_agent usage - Test orchestrator can discover and call synthesis_agent - Validate orchestrator logs show synthesis_agent execution

Document agent usage and integration (1 hour) - Update docs/architecture/3-1-agentic-workflow-guide.md with synthesis_agent example - Document synthesis_agent signature and SynthesisResult format - Add code example showing complete 3-agent workflow - Document multi-source aggregation patterns and best practices

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Synthesis agent defined with @tool decorator per AWS Strands framework - Agent decorated with @tool decorator from AWS Strands - Agent signature follows Strands tool conventions - Agent registered with orchestrator as callable tool - Agent accepts List[AgentResult] from upstream agents (retrieval + analysis)

Agent aggregates multi-source results into natural language summary - Input: retrieval_results (List[DocumentChunk]), analysis_results (List[AnalysisResult]), original_query (str) - Output: JSON-serialized final answer with reasoning steps and citations - Maintains semantic coherence across multiple information sources - Preserves source attribution from both retrieval and analysis agents

Agent uses Claude Sonnet for high-quality synthesis with structured prompts - Calls Claude Sonnet via shared client from raglite/shared/clients.py - Structured prompts ensure factual accuracy and citation preservation - Reasoning includes explanation of how sources were combined - Error handling for LLM API failures (return error metadata)

Agent tested with multi-source inputs (unit tests) - Unit test validates synthesis of retrieval + analysis results - Unit test validates source citation formatting and preservation - Unit test validates consistency with original query intent - Unit test validates handling of conflicting information from sources - Mocked Claude API prevents external dependencies - Test execution time <100ms (framework overhead only)

Agent integrates in complete 3-agent workflow (integration test) - Integration test executes Retrieval → Analysis → Synthesis full workflow - Test uses real Qdrant instance (requires docker-compose up) - Test validates complete workflow produces coherent final answer - Test validates execution time <8s for full 3-agent workflow - Test validates all source citations preserved in final output

constraints.constraint: Follow AWS Strands @tool decorator pattern established in Stories 3.1-3.3. Agent must be async function returning JSON-serialized output.
Use shared Claude client from raglite/shared/clients.py. Do NOT create new client instances - import get_claude_client() and call existing client.
Use Claude Sonnet (claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022) for synthesis, NOT Claude Haiku. Quality > speed trade-off justified for final synthesis.
File must be raglite/agentic/agents/synthesis_agent.py. Model must be SynthesisResult in raglite/agentic/state.py. Follow established naming conventions.
Unit tests must execute <100ms (mocked Claude API). Integration tests budget ~$0.15 per run (real Claude Sonnet calls). Target 8 unit tests.
Agent execution time: <1.2s p50, <2.0s p95 (per NFR5). Full 3-agent workflow: <8s total (validated in integration tests).
Follow error_handler.py patterns. Catch exceptions, return error metadata (don't crash). Support graceful degradation (NFR24).
Use structured logging with logger.info("Synthesis agent called", extra={...}). Include agent_type, query, execution_time_ms in metadata.
Target ~60-80 lines in synthesis_agent.py. ~15 lines for SynthesisResult model in state.py. Keep implementation concise.

interface.name: synthesis_agent
interface.signature: @tool async def synthesis_agent( retrieval_results: List[dict], # List[DocumentChunk] serialized analysis_results: List[dict], # List[AnalysisResult] serialized query: str, context: Optional[str] = None ) -> str: # JSON string with SynthesisResult
interface.notes: Must accept JSON dicts (Strands requirement) and return JSON string. Deserialize inputs to Pydantic models internally. Serialize SynthesisResult to JSON for return.

interface.name: SynthesisResult
interface.signature: class SynthesisResult(BaseModel): answer: str # Final natural language answer reasoning_steps: List[str] # Steps taken to synthesize answer sources: List[str] # Aggregated citations from all agents metadata: Dict[str, Any] # Execution metadata (confidence, agent_count, etc.)
interface.notes: Add after AnalysisResult model (lines 23-35). Follow same structure and documentation style.

interface.name: get_claude_client
interface.notes: Import and call to get Claude API client. Do NOT create new Anthropic() instances - use shared client for connection pooling.

interface.name: StrandsOrchestrator._load_default_tools
interface.notes: Add synthesis_agent registration after analysis_agent (lines 95+). Follow pattern: try/except block, import synthesis_agent, append to _registered_tools, log registration.
